newsitem.title: SPAIN: DIVING-HIGHBOARD GOLD AT LAST FOR HEMPEL.
newsitem.headline: DIVING-HIGHBOARD GOLD AT LAST FOR HEMPEL.

text.p: Germany's Jan Hempel finally won a European highboard diving gold on Monday 10 years after taking the first of three silvers on the 10-metre board.
Hempel, who will be 26 on Thursday, had been suffering from influenza for three days, felt worse on Sunday and even considered pulling out of the competition on Monday morning
But he decided against it and was rewarded with the gold. "I'm happy it worked out at the sixth attempt," Hempel said, looking back over his European highboard campaigns.
He also claimed a rare perfect 10 mark on his way to a victory which had looked in severe jeopardy before the last round of dives in the San Pablo pool.
The gold appeared certain to fall to the German after the first three dives of the six-dive final as the crowd cheered the 10, three 9.5s and three 9.0s awarded for his armstand triple somersault.
Hempel then led by a comfortable 33.78 points from second- placed defending champion Vladimir Timoshinin of Russia, with Ukraine's Joroslav Makogin more than 11 points further adrift in third place.
But his next two efforts were indifferent, while the unheralded Makogin scored heavily in a challenge which took him within four points of the German going into the sixth and final round.
Makogin's last effort was more modest but Hempel had little scope for error as he negotiated a hugely difficult back 1-1/2 somersaults with 4-1/2 twists.

The dive was good enough, the total lifted because of the high degree of difficulty, and the former East German from Dresden was home by nine points with a score of 609.48 from the morning's four dives and the six of the afternoon final.
After taking the silver in 1987, 1989 and 1995 and bronze in 1993, he had finally added a highboard gold to the European three-metre springboard gold he won in 1993.

Timoshinin's challenge for a third European highboard gold fell apart in the last two rounds and the champion of 1991 and 1995 dropped from third to sixth overall when he completely mismanaged his entry on his final reverse 3-1/2 somersaults.
Makogin took the silver with 600.48 and Hempel's German team mate Heiko Meyer came through for the bronze with 571.44.

Russia, who had won four of the first five diving titles contested here, failed to add to their medal tally but still led the way at the end of the sixth day of the 12-day championships with nine golds out of 13.
